correctness.rationale: For all k, a shuffle puts the input in blocks [A B; C D] and the amplified output in [A B; -bar B bar A]. Both output block rows have identical operator norms, with the first bounded by the input; stacking gives the exact √2 ceiling. At k=1 the scalar quaternionic identity improves this to one. At k=2 the explicit W=[I J; J I] and Z=[I J; -J I] obey WW*=2I and Z*=Z, Z²=2Z, proving a unitary input attaining √2; direct-sum padding works for all k≥2. The algebraic witness identities were checked independently by exact symbolic code; random checks are non-proof diagnostics.

value.rationale: Sharp exact quantitative failure of unitary-preserver stability under the first nontrivial amplification: the map preserves every level-one unitary, while level two already maps a genuine unitary to an operator of norm √2, and this is the optimum at every higher level. This directly tests the structural difference between ordinary and matricial geometry for the newly classified exotic preservers, rather than rederiving a pointwise contraction.
